title: Event-driven hosted API PRD sketch - streaming events & tool orchestration
content:
Purpose:
This is a working PRD sketch for an "event-driven" Hosted API experience that treats streaming tokens, discrete tool-call lifecycle events, and typed/structured responses as first-class events. The goal is to design a low-friction SDK surface that makes tool orchestration and robust UX (partial results, recoverable failures, telemetry) easy for product teams while preserving low latency and cost controls.

Status/context (notes to self):
- Draft / brain-dump. Not yet synced with infra on streaming buffer semantics (TODO: sync with infra/serving-runtime).
- Builds on earlier streaming & tool-calling sketches but aims to unify an "event envelope" model for SDKs (JS/Python/Go).
- Primary trigger: teams are building multi-tool agents and struggling with partial tool outputs, error semantics, and keeping responses typed for downstream parsers.

High level goals:
- Provide a single API that supports: incremental token streaming, discrete tool-call events (start/arg/result/error), and structured final responses with schema validation hooks.
- SDK ergonomics: minimal callback/noise for common cases; explicit event handlers for advanced flows.
- Keep hosted cost & latency predictable: support batchable small requests and streaming fallback.
- Observability: emit normalized telemetry events for every tool call, partial stream, and final parse.

Non-goals:
- Full agent runtime with planner/actuator (we provide primitives, not a planner).
- Heavyweight codegen for schemas — simple JSON-Schema/Protobuf hints only.

User personas:
- FE engineer integrating chat-like assistant with tool execution (calendar, DB queries) – wants simple streaming messages and tool outputs stitched into chat UI.
- ML infra engineer wanting to measure tool latencies and reroute slow tools.
- Platform engineer migrating server-side LLM calls to Hosted Dedicated; needs deterministic fallback when streaming fails.

Functional requirements:
- Streaming HTTP/HTTP2 endpoint that returns an event stream of small JSON envelopes (newline-delimited).
- Envelopes include: type (token|tool_start|tool_arg|tool_result|tool_error|structured_output|checkpoint|eos), id (request-level), seq (monotonic), optional tool_id and tool_call_id for scoping.
- SDKs: default high-level helpers for "onMessage" incremental text only; advanced hooks for tool lifecycle.
- Typed output: server can emit a final structured_output envelope with content and schema_hash; SDK should optionally validate against client-provided JSON-Schema.
- Retry semantics: tool_result envelopes are idempotent; server will include idempotency tokens for retried tool calls.

Example event envelope (ndjson):
{"type":"token","id":"r123","seq":12,"text":"ing"}
{"type":"tool_start","id":"r123","tool_call_id":"t1","tool_id":"calendar.create"}
{"type":"tool_arg","id":"r123","tool_call_id":"t1","payload":"{\"time\":\"2026-01-20T15:00Z\"}"}
{"type":"tool_result","id":"r123","tool_call_id":"t1","payload":"{\"event_id\":\"evt-99\"}"}
{"type":"structured_output","id":"r123","schema_hash":"sha256:abcd","payload":"{\"intent\":\"create_event\",\"event_id\":\"evt-99\"}"}

SDK ergonomics notes (sketches):
- JS high-level (most users):
const res = await client.chat.create({messages});
res.on('message', (m)=> renderChunk(m.text)); // default only tokens
res.on('tool', (t)=> attachToolResult(t.tool_id, t.payload));
res.on('done', (final)=> renderFinal(final.payload));

- JS low-level event stream (advanced):
for await (const ev of client.chat.stream({messages})) {
  switch(ev.type) {
    case 'token': render(ev.text); break;
    case 'tool_start': showSpinner(ev.tool_id); break;
    case 'tool_result': attachTool(ev.tool_call_id, ev.payload); break;
  }
}

- Python async generator: similar semantics (async for ev in client.stream(...))
- Go: callback-based iterator with explicit Close() for resource cleanup

Design tradeoffs / rationale:
- ndjson event envelope keeps wire simple and language-agnostic. HTTP/1.1 SSE vs HTTP2 vs websocket — prefer HTTP/2 streaming and ndjson as a baseline for broad compatibility; allow websocket for extremely low-latency UIs. Need infra input.
- Emit small typed envelopes to make client stitching simple and to support incremental rendering + telemetry attribution.
- Schema hints rather than full codegen because teams want quick integration; allow optional codegen in future.

Telemetry & observability:
- Every envelope has attributes: request_id, seq, model, route, client_id, latency_ms (for tool_result), bytes.
- Events to emit server-side to Console: tool.call.started, tool.call.completed, structured_output.validated(true/false), stream.chunk.count, stream.duration_ms.
- Attach sample prompt and canonicalized prompt_hash for regression alerts.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) API prototype behind feature flag (hosted-api streaming-v2) for internal customers + solutions teams.
2) Expand to limited beta (selected external partners) — collect SDK feedback and edge cases around reconnect and resume.
3) GA: default non-breaking behavior: if client requests streaming=false, fallback to existing unified response; streaming clients opt-in.

Compatibility and fallback: 
- If SDK cannot parse an envelope, provide a raw_fallback callback and log a parse error metric.
- Resume semantics: server will persist last-ack seq per connection for short timespan (60s). If client reconnects with last_seq, server replays from next seq. This requires infra support.

Security & privacy:
- Tool arguments may contain PII; require encryption at rest + redact logs unless explicit allowlist. Provide per-tool data classification metadata in tool_start envelope.
- Authorization: same API key scoping as existing hosted endpoints; tool calls may require additional scopes.

Performance/cost considerations:
- Envelope overhead: ensure typical token envelope <= 200 bytes to avoid 2–4x token overhead. Consider optional compressed frames for high-throughput use cases.
- Batching: server should still batch token generation internally; eventization must not force single-token roundtrips.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Sequence numbers: signed vs unsigned? (Signed helps tamper detection for private-hosted deployments)
- Protocol choice: finalize HTTP2 ndjson vs SSE vs websocket after infra perf tests. (Ticket: GHD-4981)
- Reconnect/resume TTL and guarantees (exactly-once vs at-least-once semantics)
- Schema validation engine: server-side validation for structured_output? or client responsibility?

Next steps:
- Sync w/ serving-runtime on streaming wire format and resume semantics (owner: Miguel).
- Draft initial JS SDK API surface and minimal Python generator (owner: Priya).
- Implement telemetry event names in Console mapping (owner: Ethan).
- Create alpha feature flag and internal test harness for 10 internal customers.

Appendix: quick ASCII exchange (UI stitching example)
Client UI receives:
- token events -> append to typing bubble
- tool_start -> show tool spinner in UI (with tool name & mini-state)
- tool_result -> add tool card to history and attach returned payload
- structured_output -> run local validator, then map fields to UI components

Notes: this is intentionally rough. The goal is to get alignment on the envelope model and SDK ergonomics before drafting a formal PRD with thorough API reference and error codes.
